title: Set up registered agent
summary: Every state of incorporation requires a registered agent for legal documents — pick a service and designate it online.

parts.title: Choose registered agent service
parts.guidance: Compare registered-agent services for the company’s formation and qualification states. Check the designation details, consent process, legal-notice handling, account access and renewal charges. Distinguish service of legal papers from ordinary mail forwarding. Choose a provider that covers the required states and gives the company a reliable path for urgent notices before approving the purchase.

parts.title: Sign up online and designate the agent
parts.guidance: Create the company account for the purchased service and obtain the exact agent name and address required in the state record. Check whether appointment or replacement needs a separate filing. Complete the designation and fees through the entity’s authorized filing process. Verify both provider activation and registry acceptance, then test notice routing to the company’s responsible contact.

verify.how: The agent's name and Delaware address appear on the entity's record in the Division of Corporations entity search.

parts.title: Designate the agent in each additional registered state
parts.guidance: Check the agent requirements and provider coverage in each additional registration state. Use that state’s correct agent details and appointment process, with the authorized filer approving submission. Verify the accepted designation and route notices to the appropriate company contact. A service subscription elsewhere does not establish an appointment in this state.

metadata.supportReason: Registered agent services have no public signup API — the designation is an online form; provider comparison is agent work.

geoNotes.summary: No agent industry: the analog is the registered office itself — declared at (or within 30 days of) incorporation via form INC-22 to the MCA (fronted by NSWS), with the company name displayed at the premises.

The analog is the registered office: since the 2023 ECCT Act it must be an 'appropriate address' where documents reliably reach the company (PO boxes alone are out), plus a registered email — agent-provided addresses remain fine.

No registered-agent concept: the GmbH registers an inländische Geschäftsanschrift (domestic business address) in the Handelsregister where service of process is valid — keep it current via the notary when you move.

The analog is the siège social declared through the guichet unique: it can be the founder's home or a domiciliation company — the latter must hold a prefectural agrément — and changing it is a formal statuts amendment.

No registered-agent industry: the company's sede (registered office) is declared at formation in the commercial registry and service of process reaches the company there — keep it current with an online registry filing.

No registered-agent industry: the registered office address is declared in the articles filed with Corporations Canada (or the provincial registry) and must stay current — documents are served on the corporation there.
